newsitem.title: USA: September U.S. light vehicle sales rise 5.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: September U.S. light vehicle sales rise 5.7 pct.

text.p: U.S. car and light-truck sales during September totaled 1,207,100 units with all automakers reporting, a 5.7 percent increase from the 1,189,539 units sold a year earlier, based on daily selling rates.

The seasonally adjusted annual sales rate for the month was 15 million units, even with a year ago but down from 15.8 million during August 1996. The rate is calculated with seasonal factors supplied by the U.S. Commerce Department.
In the first nine months of 1996, automakers sold a total of 11,637,108 light vehicles, up 2.6 percent from the 11,290,979 in the same period of 1995.
Automakers sold 580,018 North American-built cars in the United States in September, up 2.9 percent from a year ago.
The seasonally adjusted annual rate for domestic cars was 7.2 million units, compared with 7.3 million in September 1995 and 7.4 million in August 1996.

Automakers sold 478,308 domestic light trucks in the United States during September, up 14.3 percent from a year earlier. The seasonally adjusted annual sales rate for domestic trucks was 6.0 million units, compared with 5.7 million a year earlier and 6.5 million in August.

Imported car sales totaled 116,620 units, down 6.6 percent from a year ago, with a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.45 million units. Imported truck sales fell 8.2 percent to 32,154 units for an annual rate of 380,000 units.
